requirement: Standard verification runners supplied by Agent Framework shall remain framework-owned and shall operate on the consuming project without requiring copied project-local runner forks.
Project configuration shall complete its preflight before writing files and shall fail without modifying the consuming project when an existing path conflicts with the intended scaffold.
A normal consuming-project agent shall use the consuming project's root `AGENTS.md` as its onboarding entry point rather than the framework submodule's `AGENTS.md`.
The framework base image shall contain the dependencies required to execute every standard framework verification runner.
A consuming project's development image shall be built on top of the framework base image and may add project/package dependencies without reinstalling the framework toolchain.
Project bootstrap shall be executable on a Windows host with Git and Docker without requiring host Bash, WSL, host Python, or host Linux verification tools.
Bootstrap shall preserve unresolved product decisions when those decisions are not required to establish project identity, repository shape, or another bootstrap prerequisite.
The bootstrap agent shall finish with explicit process feedback for the framework author, including encountered friction or an explicit statement that no workflow issues were found.
Bootstrap shall not strengthen a developer-supplied product goal into additional externally observable guarantees that have not already been settled.
Bootstrap shall seed the planning, contract, and evaluation document structure without creating product contracts, evaluation activities, roadmap commitments, or implementation milestones.

Project configuration shall require a project name and initial intent and shall deterministically create the project metadata, `src/` package, minimal executable scaffold, import-and-call smoke test, root README, and architecture intent baseline from those inputs.
Project configuration shall reject a project name that cannot be normalized into a valid non-keyword Python import-package identifier using the documented ASCII naming rules.
Project configuration shall support Python 3.12 and 3.14, default to Python 3.12, and use the selected version consistently in project metadata and the framework base image build.

Project configuration shall require `agent-framework/` to be an initialized Git submodule checked out at the parent repository's recorded commit while reporting local submodule modifications as a warning rather than a failure.

Project configuration shall reject unexpected consuming-root entries, allow and warn about entries matched by the seeded `.gitignore`, and otherwise permit only `.git`, `.gitmodules`, and `agent-framework` before configuration.

When no project-local Black configuration exists, the framework Black runner shall target the Python version configured by `project.python_version` rather than relying on Black's inferred future-version target.

When no project-local Ruff configuration exists, the framework Ruff runner shall not report `EXE002` solely because Windows bind-mount semantics make Python files appear executable inside the Linux development container.
The AI sanitizer shall report possible direct milestone references found outside project planning documentation as advisory review findings without making those findings a verification failure.

The traceability generator shall accept an explicitly planned `automated-test` evaluation activity without current `@covers(...)` evidence and shall report that requirement as `PLANNED-AUTOMATED` rather than missing automated evidence.
Framework categories and tools shall be discovered from validated TOML manifests rather than from a hardcoded runner inventory.
Aggregate verification shall execute configured categories in configuration order and each category shall execute its configured tools in list order.
Duplicate tool assignments within one category shall execute only their first occurrence and shall produce a warning without failing verification.
Aggregate fixing shall run every configured category's fix phase before any configured category's verification phase and shall continue after individual tool failures.
An enabled unavailable tool shall prevent verification unless the caller explicitly supplies `--ignore-unavailable`.
`toolctl.py` shall manage ordered category assignments in the machine-managed tool section of `agent-framework.toml` without changing configuration outside that section.
Tool default inspection, comparison, deployment, and forced reset shall use configuration artifacts declared by the tool bundle manifest and shall preserve unrelated project configuration.
Verification and container-build entry points shall keep only their latest complete log, use concise output by default, and print an uninterpreted output tail plus the log location on failure.
An enabled tool with no applicable input or no fix operation shall be reported as successfully skipped rather than failed.
Aggregate verification shall finish with a concise result line that reports overall success or the number of failed category runs.

Project configuration shall require an explicitly selected, discoverable bootstrap profile and the `generic` profile shall create the minimal executable scaffold with its declared initial tool assignments.
Project configuration shall seed project-owned `toolctl.py` and `run_verification.py` wrappers that forward arguments and exit status to their framework-owned implementations.
Framework-seeded project documentation shall use ordinary repository-relative Markdown links for navigation rather than requiring Sphinx or MyST navigation metadata.
The framework documentation verification category shall lint project-owned Markdown and validate repository-local Markdown links without requiring network access.
Framework-seeded `tests/util/contract.py` shall be compatible with the framework's Ruff and Pyright verification policies without requiring a consuming-project-specific suppression or rewrite.

The Agent Framework repository shall provide a repository-only pre-commit gate that runs complete framework verification in the controlled Docker environment and shall not seed that hook into consuming projects.
